title: UV sensitive vision in cardinals and tanagers is ubiquitous
why: Partial SWS1 opsin sequences across Cardinalidae and Thraupidae; says all studied have UVS-type SWS1. The abstract page did not show whether Thraupis was sampled. A gene survey, so it would give a predicted pigment class only.

authors: Talarico F, Koçak Y, Macirella R, Sesti S, Yüksel E, Brunelli E
title: Eye morphology in four species of tiger beetles (Coleoptera: Cicindelidae)
why: Compound-eye ommatidia density and facet size in four tiger beetle species, by sex. The abstract does not name the species, so it is not known whether Cicindela is among them.

authors: Schiviz AN, Ruf T, Kuebber-Heiss A, Schubert C, Ahnelt PK
title: Retinal cone topography of artiodactyl mammals: influence of body height and habitat
why: Cited by the 2024 Cervidae visual ecology review as the source for a moose retinal cone streak and tapetum extension; cone topography of many artiodactyls, so it may also give moose peak cone density for an acuity estimate.

authors: Stavenga DG, Kinoshita M, Yang EC, Arikawa K
title: Retinal regionalization and heterogeneity of butterfly eyes
why: Survey of butterfly eyes from several families by epi-illumination (facet diameter, interommatidial angle, eye parameter); the abstract names no species, so the full text is needed to see whether Maniola, Battus or other genera on the queue are included.

authors: Kwak MJ, Je SM, Cheng HC, Seo SM, Park JH, Baek SG, Khaine I, Lee T, Jang J, Li Y, et al.
title: Night light-adaptation strategies for photosynthetic apparatus in yellow-poplar (Liriodendron tulipifera L.) exposed to artificial night lighting
why: Diurnal and seasonal patterns of photosynthesis and PSII in tulip tree under night lighting; the only Liriodendron light-response study found. Abstract could not be read.
